Share on X Telegram Tuesday’s US elections have produced a historic milestone, with four Black politicians winning gubernatorial races, paving the way for multiple elected Black governors to serve simultaneously for the first time in the country’s history.
The victories followed wins by Democratic Governor Wes Moore in Maryland, Republican Representative Byron Donalds in Florida and Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms in Georgia.
Hours later, David Crowley also secured victory in Wisconsin’s gubernatorial race, becoming the fourth Black politician to win a governorship in Tuesday’s elections.
The development marks a significant moment in American political history, as no two elected Black governors had previously served at the same time.
Before Tuesday’s victories, only three Black politicians had been elected governors in the United States.
They were Moore, who was elected governor of Maryland; Deval Patrick, a Democrat who won the Massachusetts governorship in 2006; and Doug Wilder, who made history in 1989 as the first Black governor of Virginia.
In an interview with NBC News last month, Donalds described the historic significance of his gubernatorial candidacy as “very special.”
“From a larger perspective, there’s so much that has been talked about in politics over the last couple decades around race. Obviously, the country has had some real negative parts of our history surrounding race,” he said.
“I’m humbled to be in this position, but I think it says a lot more about the state [of Florida] than it does about me.”
Meanwhile, the number of Black politicians who could join the historic group may increase, depending on the outcome of another gubernatorial contest.
Nevada Attorney General Aaron Ford, a Black Democrat, is also seeking to become governor, challenging incumbent Republican Governor Joe Lombardo.
However, several other Black candidates failed to secure victories in their respective gubernatorial contests.
In South Carolina, Democratic State Representative Jermaine Johnson lost the governorship to Republican Alan Wilson.
Similarly, Republican Representative John James lost his gubernatorial bid to Democrat Jocelyn Benson, while Minnesota State House Speaker Lisa Demuth was defeated by Democrat Amy Klobuchar.
The victories mark a significant development in the representation of Black Americans in the country’s highest state executive offices.
